_note: General Kuwaiti lexicon (model-independent), started 2026-10-10. What a Kuwaiti says, not how any model needs it spelled: that lives in a per-model map (ckkw-spelling-map.json for Genarabia Chatterbox_Kuwaiti). Use it to turn script text into natural Kuwaiti and, later, as knowledge for a general Kuwaiti model. 'say' is a rough Latin guide (g = Kuwaiti ق, ch = Kuwaiti ك/چ, y = Kuwaiti ج, ' = ع). status: confirmed = the user said or heard it; proposed = from general Kuwaiti usage, waiting for the user to confirm or correct.

fields.instead_of: MSA or other-dialect words a script may contain; replacing them is a word-choice change

يمديك.meaning: you have time to, you can

ماكو.note: مافي is also heard in Kuwait; which one Ali uses is for the user to say

أمس.source: the user: امبارح is not Kuwaiti

چذي.source: the user: كذا is Saudi; usually written جذي

ربيعي.note: a Kuwaiti would usually say ربيعي; صديقي was unsolved for the model

sounds._note: Kuwaiti pronunciation of letters in common words. Written forms stay standard; only the sound changes.

ق as g.status: confirmed for the first eight (the user's ear, tests 1 and 2)

ق stays q.rule: learned or formal words keep a real q

ك as ch.rule: ch near front vowels in many native words, never in every ك
ك as ch.status: confirmed for كم, باكر, كذا; كبيرة and كان under test

ج as y.rule: older and everyday Kuwaiti speech; many speakers also say j

الطريق.status: both heard; Ali chose الطريج in an earlier model's test (lexicon.json)

word_choice_rules: Write Kuwaiti words, not MSA or Saudi/Egyptian ones: امبارح → أمس, كذا → جذي, أبغى → أبي, مين → منو, ليه → ليش.
فقط in speech is usually بس; keep فقط only when the script is formal.
